text: Then it is said: from the occurrence of sensory contact, a cognition arises that encompasses both the commonality of oneness and the specific instance of oneness; from this, the notion of twoness is produced. Then follows the valid cognition of twoness, and subsequently, following the proof of twoness, the thought "there are two substances" arises; this is the described process of the emergence of twoness. What is the proof that this is produced by the comparative cognition of twoness? To this, the teachers say: the comparative cognition is capable of producing the notion of twoness, because its role as a mere indicator is not tenable, and it is therefore established by that [reason].
